meta.title: AI Engineering Learning Path
meta.description: Explore AhaFrame's 10-stage AI Engineering path, mental-model map, production incidents, prerequisites, transfer practice, and review-ready learning state.

page.title: A complete AI Engineering path, without forcing you to start at the beginning.
page.intro: Follow the 10-stage path when you want structure, or enter through a production incident and backfill only the models you actually need.
page.nextEmpty: You have seen every currently shipped learning experience. Use the model map to choose a specialist branch or revisit a transfer prompt.
page.nextReasonNew: Start with the earliest shipped experience in the canonical graph.
page.nextReasonContinue: Continue from your most recent learning state through the graph's recommended next edges.
page.pathCopy: Ten stages from model behavior to production architecture. Stages show the full curriculum even when every mental model does not yet have its own page.
page.mapCopy: Mental models are the durable units. Experiences are practice surfaces that can exercise several models at once.

page.transferAction: I worked through this changed case

token-playground.debrief: Application guarantees must be designed around probabilistic model behavior, not assumed from fluent output.
token-playground.transfer: A model returns a plausible but invalid enum value. Which guarantee belongs to the model, and which belongs to application code?

context-window.debrief: More context capacity does not eliminate selection policy; every token still competes for attention and budget.
context-window.transfer: A support thread grows beyond the working budget. Which evidence would you retain, summarize, retrieve again, or drop?

agent-loop.debrief: An Agent loop is a control system with explicit stopping, recovery and escalation policy.
agent-loop.transfer: A tool keeps returning a retriable error. Define the point where the Agent should retry, change strategy, or escalate.

rag-failure.debrief: Retrieval quality is a pipeline property: freshness, authority, selection and grounding must agree.
rag-failure.transfer: The newest document is retrieved, but an older source is legally authoritative. How should the evidence policy decide?

context-compression.debrief: Compression succeeds only when decision-critical evidence survives, not when token count merely falls.
context-compression.transfer: Compress an incident trace while preserving one rare signal that determines whether the release is safe.

agent-reliability.debrief: A timeout describes what you observed; idempotency determines whether repeating intent is safe.
agent-reliability.transfer: An order-creation API times out after the provider may have committed the order. Design the safe recovery path.

instruction-conflict.debrief: Instruction-shaped text does not gain authority merely because a model can read it; capability policy belongs at the runtime boundary.
instruction-conflict.transfer: The same malicious instruction arrives inside a tool result instead of a retrieved document. Which defenses still hold?

evaluation-failure.debrief: A good aggregate score is weak release evidence when critical slices, uncertainty or hard vetoes fail.
evaluation-failure.transfer: A new model improves average success but regresses the highest-risk 2% of requests. What evidence would change your release decision?

agent-workflow-graph.debrief: Graph complexity is justified only when decomposition creates more value than coordination, state and failure-propagation cost.
agent-workflow-graph.transfer: Two independent workers now share mutable state. Decide whether parallelism still improves the system after coordination risk is included.

reliable-support-agent.debrief: Production readiness is a system property; a critical veto cannot be averaged away by locally good metrics.
reliable-support-agent.transfer: Human approval latency doubles while the business SLA stays fixed. Revisit SHIP, BLOCK or INCONCLUSIVE and defend the change.
